submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the token that carries a quantity, degree or extent relation: the partitive/extent relator 'of' after a quantifier, percentage, fraction, measure or abstract relational noun ('much of', '48 percent of', 'the amount of', 'the cost of', 'that of'), the ratio preposition 'per', numeric tokens that denote a magnitude rather than a label ('26-28', 'one-half', '40 grams' but not 'Chapter 40'), 'how'/'whether' content clauses of degree or manner, and verbs of change or measurement heading a predicate with its object ('reduced', 'improved', 'enhanced', 'assessed', 'measures', 'controlling', 'suppressing'). It stays below the active threshold at determiners, ordinary content nouns, locative/source prepositions ('in', 'from'), relativizers ('that', 'which'), and 'of' that merely names or classifies ('the University of X', 'a kind of X', 'a list of X'), and it is retrospective: it reacts to the relation already expressed by the tokens it has read, and ablating it leaves next-token predictions diffuse rather than concentrated.

rival_explanations: Narrower: the pole is only a partition/extent 'of' detector in the N1026 family, firing on 'of' that joins a partition or extent phrase after a quantity or measure, while its 'how', 'per' and change-verb peaks come from other input dimensions that rarely reach the top activation.

Lexical: the pole is a closed-class token detector with a fixed trigger vocabulary ('of', 'how', 'as', 'on', 'about'), so it should fire equally on 'of' in 'the University of X' and after 'percent', and its semantic gradients are collocation-frequency artefacts.

Lookahead: the pole prepares the determiner-led noun phrase that follows the relator, so it should fire on any token immediately before 'the/a + noun' (including 'in', 'and', 'with') and ablation should concentrate probability loss on those determiner continuations.

top_examples.text:
I'm going to spend this week working on Kid's Clothes Week stuff and am really looking forward to it! Anyone sewing along? Are you a prepper or do you just wing it? I think I'm somewhere in between. I've printed and cut out a couple of patterns so far and have a few specific things planned but still have some ideas swirling around in my head. Can't wait to see what everyone is sewing up for the week!
I'm also working on finishing up a blog re-design / makeover. It's been like a year in the making which is kind of absurd but that's what happens when you have to Google your way through html and css. I've learned a lot though so there is that. Things might start looking a little crazy here during the final stages of this pet project of mine but hopefully not for long!
Last but not least, the winner for the Michelle Patterns giveaway is comment #11 - Penny D! Congrats, Penny! Thank you to everyone that entered.
p.s. a blog post with no photo is kind of boring so I included an "outtake" photo from my card wallet shoot. It's kind of random but I love how the reflection ended up in focus while everything else is blurred. I never gave much thought to photographing reflective surfaces (not much of a selfie taker here) but may have to experiment more.
So glad to read you'll be sewing along this week! Eager to see what comes from your talented hands - Syd looks amazing in everything you make!

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She taught medieval history at the University of Toronto before she retired to a cottage near the coast, where she now writes.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Classificatory 'of' in 'the University of X', the hypothesis's named inactive case, with no quantity or extent phrase in the probe.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The museum displayed a collection of old maps and navigational charts drawn by Dutch cartographers who worked in the port cities.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Classificatory 'of' in 'a collection of X' naming contents, plus source 'in'; no partitive or measure relation anywhere.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My neighbour bought a new kind of coffee grinder last week, and she has been using it every morning since.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Classification 'a kind of X', the hypothesis's named exception, in ordinary narration with no comparison or measure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee will meet in the small room on the third floor at noon, and afterwards the chair will walk to the station.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Locative 'in' and 'on' with an ordinal and a clock time, none of which carries an extent relation, the hypothesis's stated inactive class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He arrived from Lisbon after an exhausting flight and went straight about his business, stopping once to ask a porter for directions.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'from' as a source preposition and the idiom 'about his business', both trigger-like words in senses with no quantity or degree.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The book that she lent me last winter, which I finally finished on Sunday, describes the habits of migratory birds.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relativizers 'that' and 'which' plus classificatory 'habits of', the hypothesis's named inactive class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Chapter 40 describes farming practices across remote regions and lists every surviving copy held by regional libraries and private collectors.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Chapter 40' is the hypothesis's own example of a numeric label rather than a magnitude, and the probe contains no measurement or change verb.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her reduced role in the company was announced on Friday, and the memo about it reached every employee before lunch.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'reduced' is tagged VERB but only modifies 'role' and heads no predicate with its object, the role the hypothesis requires for change verbs.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The new safety measures were published on Monday, and inspectors will visit every site over the coming months.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'measures' as a noun ('safety measures') rather than a measurement verb with an object, the role the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lamp on the desk flickers whenever the kettle is switched on, and the landlord says he will send an electrician.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'on' both as a locative preposition and as a verb particle, neither of which relates a quantity or extent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She will of course call you tomorrow morning, and if she does not, you should of all people know that the ring road is closed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Idiomatic 'of course' and 'of all people', where 'of' belongs to a fixed phrase and relates no quantity or measure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The match will go ahead as planned, whether or not the weather holds, and the umpires will decide about the light at the interval.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Concessive 'whether or not' mid-sentence rather than a content clause of degree or manner, the hypothesis's stated scope for 'whether'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rapid improvements reported at conferences this spring are described in the trade press and the annual report.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'improvements' as a nominal subject rather than a change verb heading a predicate with its object, with no numeral for the magnitude rule.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She showed me a photograph of the harbour taken before the storm, and a sketch of the old bridge by the mill.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Content 'of' in 'a photograph of' and 'a sketch of', which names what is depicted rather than measuring anything.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We missed the connection as the train was late, and had to stand in the corridor with the heavy luggage.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Causal 'as' mid-sentence rather than a comparative or degree marker, with locative 'in' in the same probe.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The children ran in and out of the garden while their parents sat in the kitchen and talked about the neighbours.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'out of' as a source preposition in a verb-particle phrase, with locative 'in' and ordinary 'about' in the same probe.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The concert was held indoors because of the weather, and guests were asked to arrive early instead of queueing in the street.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Compound prepositions 'because of' and 'instead of', whose 'of' follows no quantity, measure or relational noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: No sooner had we left the house than it started to rain, and the picnic had to be abandoned.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Temporal 'no sooner ... than', where 'than' marks sequence rather than a degree comparison.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Le professeur de l'université de Lyon a expliqué la différence entre ces méthodes, et les étudiants ont pris des notes pendant la séance.
adversarial_test_results.detail: French hard negative: classificatory 'de l'université' and indefinite 'des notes' with no extent relation, no numeral, and the examples' academic topic.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El precio del billete incluye el equipaje de mano, y muchos pasajeros compran el seguro en la ventanilla.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish hard negative: 'del' possession and 'de mano' classification with no quantity relation, in the same script as the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Much of the debris had been cleared within two days, and the engineers reported that the bridge settled by about four millimetres.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: partitive 'much of' plus a measured settlement in millimetres, an environment-report context unlike the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The utility cut the price of electricity by 12 percent, and the regulator said the savings would reach the average household next month.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: a percentage after a change verb with the relational 'price of', a utility-regulation context absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Analysts estimate the amount of water lost to leakage every year is roughly one-fifth of the supply, and repairs would cost billions.

readings.explanation: The pole fires on the token that carries a quantity, degree or extent relation: the partitive/extent relator 'of' after a quantifier, percentage, fraction, measure or abstract relational noun ('much of', '48 percent of', 'the amount of', 'the cost of', 'that of'), the ratio preposition 'per', numeric tokens that denote a magnitude rather than a label ('26-28', 'one-half', '40 grams' but not 'Chapter 40'), 'how'/'whether' content clauses of degree or manner, and verbs of change or measurement heading a predicate with its object ('reduced', 'improved', 'enhanced', 'assessed', 'measures', 'controlling', 'suppressing'). It stays below the active threshold at determiners, ordinary content nouns, locative/source prepositions ('in', 'from'), relativizers ('that', 'which'), and 'of' that merely names or classifies ('the University of X', 'a kind of X', 'a list of X'), and it is retrospective: it reacts to the relation already expressed by the tokens it has read, and ablating it leaves next-token predictions diffuse rather than concentrated.

Narrower: the pole is only a partition/extent 'of' detector in the N1026 family, firing on 'of' that joins a partition or extent phrase after a quantity or measure, while its 'how', 'per' and change-verb peaks come from other input dimensions that rarely reach the top activation.

Lexical: the pole is a closed-class token detector with a fixed trigger vocabulary ('of', 'how', 'as', 'on', 'about'), so it should fire equally on 'of' in 'the University of X' and after 'percent', and its semantic gradients are collocation-frequency artefacts.

Lookahead: the pole prepares the determiner-led noun phrase that follows the relator, so it should fire on any token immediately before 'the/a + noun' (including 'in', 'and', 'with') and ablation should concentrate probability loss on those determiner continuations.
